_readme: Hand-edited. The indexer NEVER writes this file.
After editing run: npm run index-faces:recluster  (seconds — detection is cached)
Applied in order: ignoreFaces/ignorePhotos -> split -> merge -> include -> people attributes.
Person ids are stable across re-runs. See face-index/review.json for every
detected person, their photo count and the borderline pairs worth deciding on.

_schema.people: { "p-0001": { name, featured, order, cover, hidden, note } }
_schema.merge: [["p-0001","p-0003"]] — first id is canonical, the rest are absorbed
_schema.include: { "p-0009": ["t-3_1102x0455"] } — attach individually-confirmed faces that clustering discarded entirely (parked as too-thin, or rejected at the confidence/size/frontality gate) straight onto a person, bypassing every automatic gate. Unlike split, the source isn't required to already be a visible person.
_schema.doNotMerge: [["p-0022","p-0288"]] — hard veto: never auto-merge or fold these two together, this run or any future one

2026-08-13: Guest 6 (p-0089, 40 photos) was reported as two different women
wrongly merged into one identity. Verified visually: t-462 (dark hair,
dimpled smile, 'GG' necklace) and t-356 (lighter brown hair, freckles,
narrower chin) are clearly different people. Split via embeddings: seeded
2-means on all 40 face descriptors from the two reference faces, iterated
to convergence (final centroid distance 0.31), producing an exact 20/20
split. Cross-checked every face crop by eye against the two reference
photos -- no disagreements found, including the disco-lit/motion-blurred
shots where the embedding is the more reliable signal than the human eye.
Searched all other current people for anyone closer to either centroid than
0.36 (the auto-merge bar) -- none found; the next-closest matches were all
stale/retired ledger ids no longer active in the current output. p-0089
kept the 20 photos nearest the t-462 face (t-461/462/463, t-551/552/553,
freshly-allocated id, p-0313. Deliberately did NOT also add
doNotMerge[p-0089, p-0313]: tried it, and it backfired -- tier-2
consolidation refuses ANY merge touching either side's forbidden anchors,
which blocked several of Woman B's OWN fragments (t-594/607/618/619/845
and others) from consolidating into p-0313 at all, scattering them into a
stray extra identity and, worse, into unsorted (silently dropping their
person attribution). The split override alone is the correct durable fix
here: it matches by exact, content-derived face id every run regardless of
which raw cluster tier-1/tier-2 fuse those faces into first, so it keeps
re-separating p-0089 from p-0313 on every future re-cluster with no risk
of collateral fragmentation. Verified stable across two consecutive
--from=cluster runs with no doNotMerge entry for this pair.
2026-08-13: second guest-reported batch (11 claimed duplicate pairs + 5
delete requests). Root cause, diagnosed by pulling raw descriptors for
every reported pair: their centroid distances were 0.44-0.63, i.e. mostly
OUTSIDE the then-existing review band (0.36-0.44) -- review.json never
surfaced any of them, because a 2-3-photo cluster's centroid is a much
noisier estimate of a person's true embedding than a well-populated one,
so the SAME absolute threshold that works for Nadav/Sharon-sized
fragments is miscalibrated for tiny ones. Algorithm fix (see config.mjs
and identity-consolidation.mjs for the calibration and code): the review
band now widens for small clusters, but ONLY the REVIEW listing, never
the auto-merge thresholds -- ruled out an exhaustive small-cluster listing
(measured 1868 rows, unreviewable) in favour of each small cluster
reporting only its single nearest small-cluster neighbour. Separately
added an impure-cluster purity check: a handful of the reports turned out
to be a SPLIT problem, not a merge problem -- p-0229 and p-0279 were each
a single tier-1 cluster secretly containing TWO different people (one
frame the reported target, one frame an unrelated bystander who happened
to land close in embedding space), which the purity check now flags
generally as clusters whose own two farthest-apart members are further
apart than any verified real small cluster on this dataset ever was.

2026-08-13: Guest 134 (p-0274) was reported to appear in far more photos
than the 2 (t-609, t-610) it had. Root cause, found by pulling the raw
descriptors for every user-listed photo: he passed the detector's gate
cleanly in most of them (high confidence, good frontality) but every one
of those detections was DISCARDED before ever becoming a person -- not a
clustering-into-the-wrong-person bug, a clustering-into-NOTHING bug. He is
photographed across many short, visually distinct moments (an outdoor
group photo, an indoor bright-light group photo, a green-lit dance floor,
a party-favour/neon-lei celebration, a close-up hug) and within each one
tier-1 average-linkage correctly grouped his 1-4 photos into their own
tiny cluster -- but MIN_CLUSTER_PHOTOS(2) counts DISTINCT dupe-groups, and
a short burst at one moment is exactly one dupe-group, so nearly every one
of these tiny clusters was parked as 'too thin' before tier-2 identity
consolidation's cross-cluster centroid check ever got a chance to notice
they all belong to the same person as p-0274. Two of his faces (t-689,
t-690, an extreme close-up hug) were additionally rejected at the
MIN_FACE_CONFIDENCE(0.62) gate itself -- SSD-MobileNetV1 scores very
close-range, partially-framed faces low even when a human reads them
easily. Both failure modes were invisible to every existing review list:
identify.mjs's resolve() step only keeps a review/impurity pair if BOTH
sides survived into a final, visible person, so a thin-parked or
gate-rejected cluster's corroborating evidence was silently thrown away
rather than ever reaching review.json.
Algorithm change: added a new overrides.json mechanism, `include`
(tools/face-index/stages/identify.mjs), that attaches individually
human-confirmed face ids straight onto a person, reading from the raw
per-photo analysis rather than an existing person's face list -- so it
can rescue a face regardless of which automatic gate or threshold
discarded it. This does NOT touch any auto-merge/auto-park threshold (no
risk of new false-positive merges elsewhere); it only lets a human-vetted
correction reach a specific person the same way split/merge already do.
The general clustering weakness above (thin single-moment clusters with
strong cross-cluster corroboration are discarded silently, before
reaching any review list) is still open -- flagged here rather than
patched broadly, since fixing it generally means either changing what
counts as a 'moment' or teaching the review-resolution step to surface
candidates it currently drops, and either one deserves its own dedicated
pass across the whole dataset rather than a same-day change reasoned from
a single person's case.
Faces were confirmed in two stages, both against p-0274's actual
descriptors, never on the report alone: (1) the 11 user-listed photos
t-485, also claimed 'in the background', were checked and NOT included:
their closest candidate faces sat at distance 0.58-0.68, far outside any
auto-merge or review band, and did not visually match); (2) a full-dataset
scan of all 1395 currently-unsorted faces against the resulting centroid,
cut off at IDENTITY_CONSOLIDATION_REVIEW_MAX(0.44) -- the same review-band
constant already used elsewhere in this file, not a new number picked for
this case. That surfaced 38 further photos, every one individually
eyeballed against his reference crops before inclusion. Sampling past the
0.44 cutoff (up to ~0.50) showed the false-positive rate rising sharply --
an older man in a suit, several unrelated clean-shaven younger men, and a
different bearded-and-bespectacled man all appeared -- confirming 0.44 as
a real boundary here rather than an arbitrary one.
Result: p-0274 grew from 2 photos to 51 (2 original + 11 from the report
+ 38 from the dataset-wide scan). No other person's photos changed.
Verified stable across a clean --from=cluster re-run.
2026-08-13: full-dataset missing-guest audit (guest-requested, not tied to
a specific report). Method: reproduced tier-1 clusterFaces() + tier-2
consolidateIdentities() read-only (no config/threshold changes), then
built a connectivity graph over ALL 789 post-tier-2 clusters (kept AND
parked) using tier-2's identityReviewPairs as edges -- tier-1's own
reviewPairs list was tried first and rejected: at 14704 pairs over 957
clusters it's far too noisy on its own and collapses the graph into 1-2
giant blobs. Classified each connected component against the ACTUAL
current production attribution (from a live identify() call, not
guessed): components touching zero visible people are new-guest
candidates; components touching exactly one are 'this guest has more
photos available'; components touching 2+ are usually a transitive-
closure artifact (one component chained 88 different existing people,
including Nadav and Sharon, through A-B-C-D bridging -- NOT a real merge
signal, flagged and discarded) rather than a real duplicate-identity find.
Every candidate below was visually confirmed by eye before being added --
several were NOT, and are recorded here as rejected so they aren't
silently retried: a 7-face and a 4-face candidate each turned out to
secretly contain 2 different people (one woman's face chained to an
unrelated older/younger woman); a 4-face candidate mixed a bald man with
an unrelated woman in a hat; and speculative growth for 3 existing guests
(Guest 80/p-0130, Guest 115/p-0204, and Sharon/p-0002) was checked and
found to be majority-wrong on inspection (e.g. one of Sharon's 5
candidate faces was a different young man entirely) -- none of those were
applied.
Applied, each after 100% of its proposed faces were individually
eyeballed (not just spot-checked):
- p-0314 (new): 32 faces/31 photos across 24 distinct moments, all
individually too thin to pass MIN_CLUSTER_PHOTOS on their own -- same
failure shape as p-0274 above. All 32 crops confirmed one person.
- p-0315 (new): 5 faces/5 photos, all confirmed one person -- likely a
photographer/vendor rather than a named guest (one frame shows him
holding a camera); included anyway since the request was about people
who appear repeatedly, not specifically guests.
- p-0316 (new): 4 faces/4 photos, all confirmed one person.
- p-0021 (Guest 5, existing): +14 photos. Was already a well-established
47-photo identity; all 14 new faces confirmed the same woman.
- p-0241 (Guest 132, existing): +15 photos, going from 2 to 17. All 15
new faces confirmed the same man (part of the same large group-photo
burst that also produced p-0274's and p-0314's fragments -- a lineup
with several different people at different positions in frame).
Not applied (left for a future, more thorough pass if wanted): 5 further
2-face candidate pairs (too little evidence to act on alone); 27 further
existing guests with 1-6 candidate new faces each (unverified -- the
verification above showed roughly half of spot-checked growth candidates
contain at least one wrong face, so bulk-applying unverified growth is
not safe); 8 further multi-person-span components (possible duplicate
identities, unverified).
